question:
The figure consists of alternating light and dark squares. The number of dark squares exceeds the number of light squares by

[Figure 1](figures/1988_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Each row alternates colors and begins and ends with a dark square. Pair every light square with the dark square immediately to its left. These pairs use every light square exactly once and leave just the rightmost dark square unpaired in each row.

There are eight rows, so there are eight unpaired dark squares. Therefore the number of dark squares exceeds the number of light squares by \(8\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
